chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Salama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)

That he clothed the people in Iraq, and there was in the clothing a good robe. He said: Al-Husayn asked him for it, but he refused. Al-Husayn said: 'I will give you two robes in place of it.' He refused, so he kept giving him until it reached five for him. Then he took them from him, then gave him the robe, and placed the robes in his lap, and said: 'I will surely take five for one.'
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: And it has been narrated that it is disliked, and that it is better that each of them be mentioned with its price, and that is the more cautious.

key_terms.كَرَاهِيَةُ: Dislike (a legal ruling less severe than prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging one item for multiple items of different values in Islamic trade?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical flexibility of Imam Ali (AS) in commercial transactions, where he accepted a disproportionate exchange of five robes for one, demonstrating that such barter (bay' al-kil'ah) was not inherently invalid. Shaykh al-Tusi notes the scholarly divergence, with some jurists preferring the more cautious approach of specifying individual values to avoid ambiguity (gharar), reflecting the broader Shia legal principle of balancing permissibility with prudence in trade.
